title: The first friendly-versus-antagonistic discrepancy outside the consecutive-ratio family
statement:
Let $S=\{s_2,s_1\}$ with $s_2<s_1<2s_2$, and suppose

$$
\frac{s_1}{s_2}\neq\frac{k+1}{k}
$$

for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$. Let FvF and AvA denote the symmetric friendly and antagonistic self-interest games. **First-discrepancy conjecture.** There exists a heap with a friendly/antagonistic discrepancy, and the first such heap is

$$
x=(i+2)s_2+iks_1,
$$

where $i\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfies

$$
\frac{i+1}{i}>\frac{s_1}{s_2}>\frac{i+2}{k+i}.
$$

This conjecture complements the claimed no-discrepancy family above and is supported by the paper's analysis; it remains unresolved in the supplied text.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.24280

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2025).
source_name: Anjali Bhagat, Tanmay Kulkarni, Urban Larsson and Divya Murali, “Tie-breaking in self interest cumulative subtraction games”, arXiv:2510.24280 (2026).
